title: 第299章 都要满足第298章 肚子都大了
slug: 百世轮回词条无限累加
lines: 苏璃凑过去看了一眼。
“所有走廊转角加防撞护栏，舱门边缘包裹软木条，楼梯扶手高度降低到……”伊莲娜的笔尖在纸上快速划着，“甲板围栏间距不超过十二厘米，防止小孩把头伸出去。”
赛娜也探头看了看。“你这是改造船还是建幼儿园？”
“有区别吗？”伊莲娜头也没抬。
苏璃伸手把本子抽过来翻了翻。防撞、防摔、防夹、防烫，连厨房操作台的高度都标了注。
“行。”他把本子还给伊莲娜，“跟工程师说，让他们按这个改。费用走船坞维护的账。”
伊莲娜收起本子，嘴角微不可见地翘了一下。
下午，艾洛诺儿抱着一沓图纸从工坊赶过来。
她把图纸铺在干坞旁边的石桌上，银色的头发在海风里飘来飘去，不得不用手压着纸边。
“我设计了一套低功率教学回路。”她指着图纸上密麻麻的线条，“输出只有常规一阶回路的百分之一，连猫碰到都不会有反应。”
苏璃弯腰看了看。回路结构确实极度精简，用的是最基础的单线连接，节点之间留了大量冗余空间。
“这是给孩子以后用的？”
艾洛诺儿点头，耳朵尖微泛红。“等他们五六岁的时候，可以用这个学认符文。就像认字一样，先学笔画再学结构。”
赛娜从旁边伸过脑袋。“不会电到吧？”
“绝对不会。”艾洛诺儿赶紧摇头，“以太输出量比晒太阳还低，我测试过十二遍了。”
苏璃直起腰，拍了艾洛诺儿的脑袋。“留着，以后用得上。”
艾洛诺儿把图纸小心卷好，抱在怀里笑了。那笑容跟三十年前在银杏巷门口等饭吃的时候没什么两样。
“五阶后代的教育方案。”
一个声音从石台边缘飘过来。塔莉娅不知道什么时候出现在那儿，手里攥着笔，记录本翻开了新的一页。
“如果我能持续跟踪记录……”
伊莲娜连头都没回。“先签保密契约。”
塔莉娅的笔停住了。“什么？”
“所有关于孩子的记录，未经我和苏璃同意，不许外传。”伊莲娜的语气跟念合同条款似的，“违约金五千金币，或者等值材料赔偿。”
塔莉娅脸上的表情像是吞了颗酸橄榄。
苏璃看了她一眼。“别委屈了，你那三间屋子的笔记够写十本书了。孩子的事上规矩一点，不过分吧？”
塔莉娅把记录本合上，嘟囔了一句“大陆首例五阶后代的成长观察数据多珍贵你们知不知道”，转身走了。
走出三步又折回来。“契约明天签行不行？”
“行。”伊莲娜连眼都没抬。
入夜。
港口的灯塔亮了，黄色的光在水面上拉出一道长的影子。
苏璃一个人站在银杏号的甲板上。
他把手搭在船舷上，掌心贴着金属表面。微凉的触感从指尖传来，船体下面，推进核心安静地嗡鸣着，频率低得几乎听不见。
他闭上眼，把体内的以太往核心方向引了一丝。
回应来得很轻，像是被窝里翻了个身继续睡的猫。他把核心调成了休眠养护模式，让它维持最低限度的运转，靠自然吸收周围环境的游离以太来缓慢“进食”。

Su Li leaned over and took a look.
"Anti-collision guardrails are added to the corners of all corridors, cork strips are wrapped around the edges of the hatches, and the height of the stair handrails is lowered to..." Elena's pen tip quickly scratched on the paper, "The distance between the deck rails should not exceed twelve centimeters to prevent children from sticking their heads out."
Senna also looked over. "Are you renovating a ship or building a kindergarten?"
"Is there any difference?" Elena didn't even raise her head.
Su Li reached out and took out the book and flipped through it. Anti-collision, anti-fall, anti-pinch, anti-scalding, even the height of the kitchen worktop is marked.
"Okay." He returned the notebook to Elena, "Tell the engineers and let them change it according to this. The cost will be charged to the dock maintenance account."
Elena put away the notebook and raised the corners of her mouth slightly.
…
In the afternoon, Elonelle came over from the workshop holding a stack of drawings.
She spread the drawings on the stone table next to the dry dock, her silver hair fluttering in the sea breeze, and she had to press the edges of the paper with her hands.
"I designed a low-power teaching circuit." She pointed to the dense lines on the drawing. "The output is only one percent of the conventional first-order circuit. Even a cat will not react when it touches it."
Su Li bent down and took a look. The loop structure is indeed extremely streamlined, using the most basic single-wire connections, leaving a lot of redundant space between nodes.
"Is this for the child's future use?"
Elonelle nodded, the tips of her ears turning slightly red. "When they are five or six years old, they can use this to learn to recognize runes. Just like recognizing characters, learn the strokes first and then learn the structure."
Senna stretched her head from the side. "It won't be electric, will it?"
"Absolutely not." Elonelle quickly shook her head, "The ether output is lower than the sun. I have tested it twelve times."
Su Li straightened up and patted Elonelle on the head. "Keep it, you may need it later."
Elonelle rolled up the drawing carefully, held it in her arms and smiled. That smile was no different from when I was waiting for food at the gate of Ginkgo Alley thirty years ago.
"Education plan for fifth-order descendants."
A voice floated over from the edge of the stone platform. Talia didn't know when she appeared there, holding a pen in her hand and turning a new page in her notebook.
"If I can keep track..."
Elena didn't even look back. "Sign a confidentiality agreement first."
Thalia's pen stopped. "What?"
"All records about the child are not allowed to be disclosed without the consent of Su Li and I." Elena's tone was like reading out the terms of a contract. "Liquidated damages of five thousand gold coins, or equivalent material compensation."
Thalia's face looked like she had swallowed a sour olive.
Su Li glanced at her. "Don't be aggrieved. The notes in those three rooms of yours are enough to write ten books. You should be more disciplined when it comes to your children, shouldn't you go too far?"
Thalia closed the record book, muttered "Do you know how precious the growth observation data of the first fifth-level offspring in the mainland is?", turned around and left.
Take three steps and turn back. "Can the contract be signed tomorrow?"
"Okay." Elena didn't even raise her eyes.
…
At night.
The port's lighthouse was on, and its yellow light cast a long shadow on the water.
Su Li stood alone on the deck of the Ginkgo.
He put his hands on the side of the boat, his palms against the metal surface. A slightly cool touch came from the fingertips. Under the hull, the propulsion core hummed quietly, with a frequency so low that it was almost inaudible.
He closed his eyes and drew a little bit of the ether in his body toward his core.
The response came softly, like a cat turning over in bed and continuing to sleep. He put the core into dormant maintenance mode, allowing it to operate at a minimum and slowly "eating" by naturally absorbing free ether from the surrounding environment.
